source.publication: 2025 Expanded Instructions (IA 1040) and the 2025 IA 1040 Iowa Individual Income Tax Return
source.section: IA 1040 form PDF p.1 Step 3 lines a, b, d; form PDF p.2 lines 1c, 2-5, 7, 8, 11, 12; Instructions PDF p.8 Step 3; PDF p.9-10 lines 2-4; PDF p.12 line 5 ('Iowa now has a flat tax rate of 3.8%'); PDF p.18 line 12

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (you) 37,600.00 = 37,600.00. Federal taxable income = 37,600.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 - 2 x 1,600.00 for 65 or older = 2,900.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). IA 1040 filing status 2 (married filing jointly). Step 3 line a personal credits 2 x 40.00 = 80.00; line b 2 x 20.00 = 40.00 (65 or older on or before January 1, 2026; nobody blind); line c no dependents; line d and line 8 = 120.00. Line 1c federal AGI 37,600.00; line 2 federal taxable income 2,900.00. Schedule 1: no additions or subtractions. Schedule 1 line 21 net modifications = 0.00; line 3 = 0.00. Line 4 Iowa taxable income = 2,900.00 + (0.00) = 2,900.00. Line 5 tax = 3.8% x 2,900.00 = 110.20; line 7 = 110.20. Line 11 total credits 120.00; line 12 = 110.20 - 120.00, below zero, so enter 0.00 (non-refundable; expected credits shows the 110.20 used). State income tax 0.00 (no line 13-17 credits; line 19 school district or EMS surtax is local, not computed). The form allows whole-dollar rounding; expected keeps the cents. Low-income exemption and alternate tax (PDF p.10-13): line 4 2,900.00 + federal deduction 34,700.00 = 37,600.00, against 32,000.00: not exempt; alternate tax 4.3% x (37,600.00 - 32,000.00) = 240.80, not smaller than the 3.8% tax. The tax of 110.20 is over 100.00 (one 65 credit) and under 120.00 (two), so each spouse's own 65 credit counts.
accepted_approximations: School district and county EMS surtaxes (a percentage of the tax, form line 19) are local and out of scope (issue #1).
